prompt: The first MGET succeeds and the second fails. Why does the second MGET fail?
explanation: MGET is a multi-key command, so every key must live in one slot. The braces in {user:42}:name and {user:42}:email make both keys hash on the tag user:42 — same slot, success. Without braces the full keys user:42:name and user:42:email hash independently and can land in different slots, which the cluster reports as CROSSSLOT.
code:
MGET {user:42}:name {user:42}:email
1) "Ada"
2) "ada@example.com"
MGET user:42:name user:42:email
(error) CROSSSLOT Keys in request don't hash to the same slot

options.text: Without hash tags the two keys hash to different slots, and multi-key commands require one slot
The first MGET changed the keys' slots as a side effect
MGET is unsupported in cluster mode and only works behind Sentinel
The email key expired between the two commands
